The Clinical Dietitian will provide specialized nutrition assessment, counseling, and medical nutrition therapy within an integrative and functional medicine model of care. The Clinical Dietitian will evaluate patients’ nutritional status, dietary patterns, lifestyle factors, health history, lab findings, and other relevant clinical parameters to develop individualized, evidence-informed nutrition interventions designed to support optimal health, prevent and manage chronic disease, and promote whole-person wellness.

Working collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team of physicians and other health professionals, the Clinical Dietitian will integrate nutrition science with the principles of integrative and functional medicine to identify and address nutrition-related contributors to health and disease. Responsibilities include conducting comprehensive nutrition assessments; reviewing and interpreting relevant lab and clinical data; developing individualized nutrition care plans; providing one-on-one nutrition consultations and education; and supporting patients in implementing sustainable dietary and lifestyle changes.

The Clinical Dietitian will also develop and facilitate group nutrition education programs and classes to promote health literacy, disease prevention, and self-management. Services provided by the Clinical Dietitian may include, but are not limited to, comprehensive dietary and nutrition assessments, individualized medical nutrition therapy, nutrition counseling and education, therapeutic dietary recommendations, and collaboration in the development of comprehensive integrative and functional medicine care plans.
